intro: Palagiano's tree is the Pino di Lenne, an Aleppo pine in the pinewood of Marina di Lenne on the Ionian coast, 4.45 metres round and 22 metres tall in Puglia's register of monumental trees. A national report on the dunes here calls it more than 600 years old. It stands about 20 metres from the road through the pines, inside the Stornara state nature reserve, and the beach in front of it carries its name.
meta_description: The Pino di Lenne, a giant Aleppo pine in the Marina di Lenne pinewood near Palagiano, 4.45 m round: where it stands and how to find it.
question_meta: The Pino di Lenne is a monumental Aleppo pine in the Marina di Lenne pinewood near Palagiano, about 20 metres from the road behind the beach.
question_answer: The tree to see near Palagiano is the Pino di Lenne, an Aleppo pine 4.45 metres round and 22 metres tall in the pinewood behind the Lenne beach on the Ionian coast. A national report calls it more than 600 years old. It stands about 20 metres from the road through the pines and costs nothing to visit.
question_context: Marina di Lenne is the coast of Palagiano on the Gulf of Taranto, about 7 kilometres from the town. Behind the beach a pinewood of Aleppo pine runs along the dunes, part of the Stornara state nature reserve, with juniper on the sand nearer the sea. Puglia's register of monumental trees lists one tree here, the Pino di Lenne, 4.45 metres round and 22 metres tall. A national report on restoring the dunes of Chiatona and Lenne calls it enormous and more than 600 years old, and says some consider it the oldest Aleppo pine in Europe; it does not say how the age was found. The beach in front of it is named after it. The tree stands about 20 metres from the road that runs through the pinewood, so a short walk from where you park is enough. No source sets out rules for walking in this part of the reserve, so keep to the tracks and off the dune plants. There is no public transport to the beach that we could find; by car or bike it is about 15 minutes from Palagiano.

faq.q: How old is the Pino di Lenne?
faq.a: A national report on the Lenne dunes calls it more than 600 years old and says some consider it the oldest Aleppo pine in Europe. It gives no basis for the figure, and nobody has dated the tree.

faq.q: How do you get to the Pino di Lenne?
faq.a: Drive or cycle from Palagiano to Marina di Lenne, about 7 kilometres. The tree stands in the pinewood behind the beach, about 20 metres from the road through the pines.

trees.verify_notes: Register: Pinus halepensis, girth 445 cm, height 22 m, locality 'Pino di Lenne', GIS point 40.518883,17.029358. ISPRA national restoration report (Repertorio nazionale degli interventi di ripristino, scheda 6a Puglia, seen in the PDF text): 'enorme e plurisecolare (oltre 600 anni) Pino di Lenne, per alcuni il piu vecchio esemplare di pino d'Aleppo d'Europa'. The 600-year figure is that report's claim with no stated basis; a 445 cm girth is consistent with a very old Aleppo pine but the figure is not independently verified, state it as the report's. PIN: iNaturalist obs 263644294 by valentino_traversa, 2025-03-02, GPS accuracy 4 m, at 40.5188909,17.0286096, description 'Il Pino di Lenne, albero monumentale con oltre 400 cm di circonferenza', taxon Pinus halepensis; that GPS fix labelled for the tree is the confirmed pin and also the recent alive check. It sits about 63 m west of the register point; the register point is the less exact one. Dune behind the pinewood has juniper stands; the area is SIC IT9130006 Pinete dell'Arco ionico.
trees.story:
A national report on restoring Puglia's coastal dunes calls this Aleppo pine more than 600 years old, and adds that some consider it the oldest of its kind in Europe. The report does not say how that age was reached, so take it as the report's number rather than a measured one. What anyone can see is the trunk. Puglia's register of monumental trees gives it 4.45 metres round and 22 metres tall, and the beach in front of it carries its name, the Spiaggia Pino di Lenne.

It grows in the pinewood of Marina di Lenne, on the Ionian coast below Palagiano, inside the Stornara state nature reserve, where pines stand behind the dunes and juniper holds the sand closer to the sea. This is the trunk people walk in to find, and a naturalist who photographed it in March 2025 recorded it as a monumental tree more than four metres round.

It stands about 20 metres from the road that runs through the pinewood, so a short walk from the car is enough. No source sets out rules for walking in this part of the reserve, so keep to the tracks and leave the dune plants where they grow.
trees.how_to_recognise: You can recognise it as the biggest pine in the Lenne pinewood, its trunk more than four metres round, about 20 metres from the road behind the beach.
